Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded $82.39 Million in Net Outflows, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Saw $69.68 Million in Net Outflows on October 16 (ET)

On October 16 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded total net outflows of $82.39 million, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $71.78 million in net outflows. Highlight Clip: Star Xu: Bitcoin Nearly Died Several Times, but Crypto Emerged Stronger

Star Xu: Bitcoin Nearly Died Several Times, but Crypto Emerged Stronger

In an interview on the New Era Finance Podcast, OKX founder and CEO Star Xu recalled Bitcoin's early forks and hash power attacks, the collapse of Mt. Gox, disagreements over scaling, and the later FTX incident. He said Bitcoin had nearly "died" several times and that resolving industry crises could take months or even a year. In his view, once those problems are resolved, the industry becomes better, bigger, and stronger than before.

Cobo Wallet, One of the Early Crypto Wallet Apps Launched by F2Pool Co-Founder, to Shut Down

Digital asset custody provider Cobo announced that its Cobo Wallet App will shut down on December 1 as part of a strategic business adjustment. Users must withdraw all assets by November 30 at 11:59 PM (UTC+8). Any remaining assets will incur a monthly management fee of 2%, with a minimum charge of $100. Accounts holding less than $100 will have their entire remaining balance deducted. The first fee will be charged on January 1, 2027, and fees will continue until all assets are withdrawn or depleted.

CoinShares: Hot CPI Drives $434M Digital Asset Fund Outflows

CoinShares said U.S. September CPI rose 3.7% year-on-year, above the 3.6% forecast, while retail sales increased 0.8% versus 0.3% expected. The stronger data pushed rate expectations more hawkish, with global digital asset investment products seeing $434 million in outflows so far this week. CoinShares said Bitcoin’s near-term setup remains difficult rather than fundamentally bearish. — link

OKX CMO Haider Rafique Plans to Leave by End of 2026

OKX Global Managing Partner and CMO Haider Rafique plans to leave by the end of 2026, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Rafique joined OKX in March 2020, led the exchange’s rebranding, and drove partnerships including with the McLaren F1 team and the Tribeca Film Festival. He also helped facilitate Intercontinental Exchange’s $200 million strategic investment in OKX in March, which valued the exchange at $25 billion. Both OKX and Rafique declined to comment. — link
